solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Red-top, to some Londoners, spouted fashionable nonsense endlessly (7,3)

indicatorNotes.spouted: something spouted is spoken out, so we want the sound of the word, not its spelling
indicatorNotes.endlessly: the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: fashionable = current, spelt as the dried fruit
BUNK = nonsense, with its last letter gone

annotation.surface: A snobbish swipe at a tabloid that talks trendy rubbish.
annotation.walkthrough: A red-top is a British tabloid, here The Sun; in Cockney rhyming slang, spoken by some Londoners, a currant bun means the Sun.
annotation.definitionFit: Cockney rhyming slang turns 'Sun' into 'currant bun', and The Sun is the best-known red-top tabloid.

entries.clue: Arrest tense Egyptian of non-Arab descent (4)

blocks.note: to cop someone is to arrest them
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

annotation.surface: A tense Egyptian being arrested.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Arrest' and 'tense' look like a description of an uneasy suspect, but each is just a short piece of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: The Copts are Egyptian Christians descended from the pre-Arab population.

entries.clue: Censure salesman over cover for household contents (7)

indicatorNotes.over: in a down clue, 'over' puts the first piece above the next

blocks.note: a rep is a sales representative
a roof covers a house and everything in it

annotation.surface: A salesman is criticised over a home contents insurance policy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cover for household contents' reads as insurance jargon, but here it is simply the thing on top of a house.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain noun synonym: both words name a telling-off, as in 'a look of reproof'.

entries.clue: In person, advanced, frail, ageless eccentric (2,5,2,4)

indicatorNotes.eccentric: eccentric means off-centre and odd, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for advanced
the remaining anagram letters

annotation.surface: A description of someone old, weak and yet somehow timeless and odd.
annotation.walkthrough: The run of adjectives looks like a portrait of an elderly eccentric, but 'eccentric' is the instruction and the portrait is just letters.
annotation.definitionFit: To turn up as large as life is to appear in person, unmistakably there.

entries.clue: Pounds through Trump’s nonsense? (6)

blocks.note: thro' is the short spelling of through
BS, short for bullshit, is the American word for nonsense

annotation.surface: A jab at money being squandered on a president's rubbish.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pounds' looks like British money; it is the verb, as a heart pounds. Trump stands in for American usage, where nonsense is BS.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym for a heartbeat or headache beating hard, both in the third person.

entries.clue: How and where rampant beasts might be indignant (2,2,4)

annotation.definition2: How and where rampant beasts might be

blocks.clueFragment: How and where rampant beasts might be
blocks.note: a rampant lion rears up, and it is found in coats of arms
the plain sense: angrily protesting

annotation.surface: Wild animals on the loose are furious.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rampant' is heraldry: a beast standing on its hind legs. 'How' it stands is UP, and 'where' it appears is IN ARMS, on a coat of arms.
annotation.definitionFit: People who are up in arms are indignant and protesting.

entries.clue: Eastern prince not to back (4)

indicatorNotes.back: to go back is to go the other way, so the word is read from its end to its start

blocks.note: a door that is 'to' is closed; one not to is ajar

annotation.surface: An Eastern prince who refuses to support something.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Not to back' reads as a refusal to support, but 'to' is the old sense of a door pushed shut.
annotation.definitionFit: A title from India, so 'Eastern' places it; a raja ruled a princely state.

entries.clue: American group working for freedom (7)

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for American
a band is a group
a machine that is on is working

annotation.surface: A US activist organisation campaigning for liberty.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a civil-rights group; 'freedom' is the noun abandon, as in dancing with abandon.
annotation.definitionFit: The noun sense, not the verb: to dance 'with abandon' is to dance with complete freedom from restraint.

entries.clue: Poised for action in drunken earthy date (2,3,5)

indicatorNotes.drunken: a drunk staggers about, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the anagram letters

annotation.surface: Someone raring to go on a boozy, rather crude night out.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a racy evening; 'drunken' is the only instruction and the rest is fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom, originally military: a rifle held at the ready is poised to fire.

entries.clue: Widely admired tree grabs you (7)

indicatorNotes.grabs: the tree takes hold of the next piece, so it goes inside

blocks.note: the poplar is a tree
U is text-speak for you

annotation.surface: A much-loved tree catches hold of the passer-by.
annotation.walkthrough: 'You' becomes U, the text-message spelling, which the setter can use without warning.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain adjective synonym: liked by many people.

entries.clue: Tick insect scratching City worker? (7)

indicatorNotes.scratching: to scratch something is to cross it out, so these letters are removed

blocks.note: INSECT with EC, the City of London's postcode, removed
a worker is an ant, the classic crossword worker

annotation.surface: A bug scratching away at a stockbroker.
annotation.walkthrough: 'City worker' looks like a banker, but it splits: the City is EC, the postcode of London's financial district, and the worker is an ANT.
annotation.definitionFit: A tick is a moment, an instant, as in 'back in a tick'.

entries.clue: Musician’s periods of heavy drinking in Germany (7,6)

blocks.note: a session is a long bout of drinking
in stays as itself
GER is the abbreviation for Germany

annotation.surface: A musician's beer-fuelled binges in Germany.
annotation.walkthrough: In British slang a session is a long drinking bout; the ’s is 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A session singer is a vocalist hired to sing on other people's recordings.

entries.clue: What’ll relieve tension in dispute about bishop appearing in whiskey promos (5,5)

indicatorNotes.about: about means turned round, so the word is reversed
indicatorNotes.appearing in: the bishop shows up inside the next word

blocks.note: a row is a dispute
rye is an American whiskey
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
ads are promotions

annotation.surface: A church leader stars in whisky adverts to ease a quarrel.
annotation.walkthrough: The first 'in' is only a link, and 'whiskey' with an E hints at the American spirit, rye, rather than Scotch.
annotation.definitionFit: Worry beads are a string of beads fingered to calm the nerves.

entries.clue: Fight stops early enough (3)

indicatorNotes.stops early: the word ends before its last letter

blocks.note: DUEL = fight, with its last letter lost

annotation.surface: A bout halted in good time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Enough' works as due does in 'with due care': as much as is needed.
annotation.definitionFit: Due care is sufficient care, so due can mean enough.

entries.clue: Introduction heralds FBI agent hero? (7,3)

indicatorNotes.heralds: a herald goes before, so the first piece comes before the second

blocks.note: a lead-in is an introduction
a G-man is an FBI agent

annotation.surface: A dramatic entrance announcing a heroic federal agent.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: the hero of a film is usually played by its leading man.
annotation.definitionFit: The leading man plays the male lead, typically the hero.

entries.clue: Slippery sort pens following pages on one high-minded engineer (6)

indicatorNotes.pens: to pen is to enclose, so the eel goes round the rest
indicatorNotes.on: placed after, so ONE comes first and the pages follow

blocks.note: slippery as an eel
I is the Roman numeral one
ff. = and the following pages

annotation.surface: A sly character writes after reading on, about an idealistic engineer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'High-minded' is a joke: Gustave Eiffel built the Eiffel Tower, so his mind ran to great heights.
annotation.definitionFit: Gustave Eiffel was the engineer behind the very tall tower in Paris.

entries.clue: Pieces inspiring AC/DC in superb atmosphere (8)

indicatorNotes.inspiring: to inspire is to breathe in, so the pieces take the next part inside
indicatorNotes.in: the result goes inside the next word

blocks.note: chess pieces are men
AC/DC is slang for bisexual
ace = superb

annotation.surface: Tracks that inspired a rock band create a great vibe.
annotation.walkthrough: AC/DC looks like the rock band or electric current; it is old slang for someone who swings both ways. 'Pieces' are chessmen, not music tracks.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the mood or feel of a place.

entries.clue: Stole loadsamoney having pinched fine wine (8)

indicatorNotes.having pinched: the pile has taken the next letter inside it

blocks.note: a pile is a fortune
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
red is wine

annotation.surface: A rich man who has nicked a good bottle.
annotation.walkthrough: Loadsamoney was a 1980s British comedy character who waved wads of cash; here the word just means a fortune. 'Pinched' tempts as the definition, but it is the container instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A past-tense synonym: pilfering is petty stealing.

entries.clue: Drink I’d sent over before matches, say, held back (8)

indicatorNotes.sent over: turned over, so the letters run backwards
indicatorNotes.before: 'before' in time means earlier, so in the answer this piece is written earlier than the next
indicatorNotes.held back: held backwards, so these letters are reversed

blocks.note: I'd written without its apostrophe
to match is to fit
e.g. = for example, say

annotation.surface: Someone sends back a drink before a fixture is postponed.
annotation.walkthrough: Both pieces go backwards: ID gives DI, and FITS EG gives GESTIF.
annotation.definitionFit: A digestif is a drink taken after a meal to aid digestion.

entries.clue: Book pioneering prog rock band (7)

blocks.note: the first book of the Bible
the band of Peter Gabriel and Phil Collins

annotation.surface: A book about the band that pioneered progressive rock.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pioneering' hints at beginnings, the literal meaning of genesis, though here it belongs to the band.
annotation.definitionFit: Genesis is both the Bible's opening book and an English progressive rock band.

entries.clue: Followed focus of friendly, retiring god (6)

indicatorNotes.focus of: the focus is the centre, so take the middle letters
indicatorNotes.retiring: going back, so the word is reversed

blocks.note: the two middle letters of FRIENDLY
deus is Latin for god

annotation.surface: A shy, sociable god was tailed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' looks like shy or going to bed; it means backing off, so DEUS reverses.
annotation.definitionFit: A past-tense synonym in the sense of coming after as a result.

entries.clue: Open at lunch breaks (7)

indicatorNotes.breaks: broken up, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the anagram letters

annotation.surface: A shop sign: open during the lunch break.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Breaks' pairs with 'lunch' to make a lunch break; it is the instruction to rearrange the words before it.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb synonym, specifically by lifting a door's catch.

entries.clue: Obsolete hand tool leaving no split nuts (3,3)

indicatorNotes.leaving: the named letters are left out
indicatorNotes.nuts: crazy, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: HAND TOOL minus N and O, which are split up in it

annotation.surface: An outdated tool that won't come apart.
annotation.walkthrough: 'No split' means the N and O removed are not together: the N comes from HAND and the O from TOOL.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal idiom for anything so familiar it has gone out of date.

entries.clue: Sister taking seconds to insert subcutaneous injection (3)

indicatorNotes.seconds: take the second letter of each of the following words

blocks.note: the second letters of iNsert, sUbcutaneous, iNjection

annotation.surface: A nurse-nun pauses briefly to give a jab under the skin.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Seconds' reads as a moment's pause; it means second letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Sister is the title given to members of a religious order of women.

entries.clue: Certain signs regularly ignored before sick twists in story (10)

indicatorNotes.before: 'before' in time means earlier, so this piece is written earlier than the next
indicatorNotes.twists: turned round, so the letters run backwards
indicatorNotes.in: the result goes inside the next word

blocks.note: the second and fourth letters of sIgNs
a fable is a story
ill = sick

annotation.surface: Omens are dismissed before a story takes grim turns.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Signs' looks like omens, but only its even letters are wanted; 'regularly' means every other letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Infallible means never wrong, so certain.

entries.clue: Privileged American supposedly lived quietly (4)

blocks.note: was = existed, lived
p (piano) is the musical term for quietly

annotation.surface: A rich American is said to have lived a quiet life.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Supposedly' belongs to the definition: a WASP, White Anglo-Saxon Protestant, is stereotyped as privileged.
annotation.definitionFit: WASP names the white Protestant elite, supposedly America's privileged class.

entries.clue: One manipulating currency reduced by large amount (7)

indicatorNotes.reduced: cut short, so the last letter goes
indicatorNotes.by: next to, so the pieces sit side by side

blocks.note: a mass is a large amount
EURO without its last letter

annotation.surface: A currency speculator cuts his holdings by a huge sum.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Manipulating currency' reads as financial fraud; the definition stops at 'One manipulating', someone who works muscles.
annotation.definitionFit: A masseur manipulates the body with his hands.

entries.clue: Meal’s gamey stuffing in cut of beef? (4,3)

indicatorNotes.stuffing in: the stuffing is what is inside, so take the middle letters

blocks.note: game that is high is strong-smelling
STEAK is a cut of beef; its inside is TEA

annotation.surface: A dish of strong-tasting game stuffed into beef.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags steak as one example of a cut of beef. High tea is an early-evening British meal with a cooked dish and tea.
annotation.definitionFit: High tea is a meal taken in the late afternoon or early evening.

entries.clue: Layer containing sulphur turned yellow in parts (4)

indicatorNotes.containing: the layer holds the next letter inside it
indicatorNotes.turned: turned round, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: a hen lays eggs
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

annotation.surface: A stratum with sulphur in it has gone yellow in places.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Layer' looks like a stratum of rock; it is one that lays, a hen. 'In parts' marks the word as regional: nesh is northern English dialect for soft or cowardly.
annotation.definitionFit: Nesh, in some regional dialects, means feeble or faint-hearted, so yellow.

entries.clue: I sorted out joint position for top hack (10)

indicatorNotes.out: out of order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the anagram letters
the hip is a joint

annotation.surface: Someone boasts of fixing a shared post fit for a top reporter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sorted out' looks like a single phrase; 'out' alone is the instruction, and 'sorted' is part of the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: The editorship is the job of the top journalist, a hack being a reporter.
